analysis_review: Phasmophobia is exactly the kind of ghost-hunting chaos I want. The problem is that I have no friends to play it with. Which is rude, because this game is clearly built for group panic. I want to walk into a haunted house with a flashlight, a dream, and the confidence of someone who has watched way too much Sam and Colby. I want to ask ghosts disrespectful questions, immediately regret it, and then scream because something moved in the kitchen. The whole setup is so good. You gather evidence, use equipment, watch for signs, try to figure out what kind of ghost you are dealing with, and then attempt to leave before it turns your investigation into a funeral announcement. It is creepy, funny, stressful, and so much better when everyone is panicking together. One person is trying to be serious. One person is already hiding in the van. One person is yelling the ghost’s name like they have never heard of consequences. That is the dream. Even without a full group, I still love the idea of it. The atmosphere is tense, the ghost mechanics are fun, and every investigation feels like it could go from “we are professionals” to “absolutely not, goodbye” in half a second. Phasmophobia lets me live my Sam and Colby dreams, or at least it would if my friends would get their lives together and play with me. Until then, I am just standing outside the haunted house with equipment, trust issues, and no backup.
